title: Bronze kingdom (Greece) to rule over all the earth
summary: The image's bronze belly and thighs stand for a third empire after Babylon and Persia. Greece under Alexander took over the Persian realm. Johnson dates the end of Persia to 326 BC (secular: Gaugamela, 331 BC).

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), period headings (book text past c. 711 BC not readable; no item numbers)

title: Iron kingdom (Rome) to break and crush all
fulfilment: History: Pompey annexes Syria and takes Jerusalem
summary: The iron legs stand for a fourth empire, strong as iron and crushing the others. Rome absorbed the Greek kingdoms, and Pompey took Jerusalem. Johnson dates Rome's period from 64 BC.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), period headings (book text past c. 711 BC not readable; no item numbers)

title: Leopard with four wings: Greece's swift conquest
summary: The third beast, a winged leopard, pictures a kingdom that would conquer with great speed. Alexander took the whole Persian Empire in about a decade.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), period headings (book text past c. 711 BC not readable; no item numbers)

title: Leopard's four heads: Greek empire in four parts
summary: The leopard's four heads foretold a fourfold split of the Greek kingdom. After Alexander died it settled into four realms under Cassander, Lysimachus, Seleucus and Ptolemy.

title: Fourth beast, iron teeth: Rome devours the earth
fulfilment: History: Roman conquest of the East
summary: A terrifying fourth beast with iron teeth would crush all the earth. Rome took over the Greek kingdoms and Judea. The ten horns and little horn are still to come.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), period headings (book text past c. 711 BC not readable; no item numbers)

title: Goat from the west sweeps without touching ground
summary: A goat from the west comes so fast it seems not to touch the ground. Gabriel names it Greece (8:21). Alexander's army moved from Macedonia into Asia at astonishing speed.

title: Goat breaks the ram's two horns (Greece defeats Medo-Persia)
summary: The goat attacks the two-horned ram, named as Media and Persia, and tramples it. Alexander defeated Darius III in three battles and ended the Persian Empire. Johnson dates this to 326 BC; secular dating has 331 BC.

title: Great horn broken at the height of its strength
summary: When the goat was strongest its great horn would be broken. Alexander died suddenly in Babylon, at the peak of his power, aged about 32 (traditionally 10 or 11 June 323 BC).

title: Four horns toward the four winds replace the great horn
summary: Four notable horns would rise in place of the broken horn, but without its power. Alexander's generals divided his realm into four kingdoms, none as strong as his.

title: Judgment on Hadrach, Damascus and Hamath
summary: Zechariah announces the word of the LORD against the Syrian cities of Hadrach, Damascus and Hamath. After Issus, Alexander's forces took Damascus and the Syrian interior.

title: Tyre's wealth cast into the sea and the city burned
fulfilment: History: Alexander's seven-month siege of Tyre
summary: Tyre had walled itself in and piled up silver and gold, but the Lord would strike her power in the sea and burn her. Alexander besieged island Tyre for seven months and destroyed it.

title: Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron and Ashdod humbled; Gaza's king perishes
fulfilment: History: Alexander takes Gaza and executes Batis
summary: The Philistine cities would see Tyre fall and tremble, and Gaza would lose its king. Alexander stormed Gaza after a two-month siege and killed its commander Batis. The other cities submitted.

title: God will encamp about His house: Jerusalem spared
summary: God promised to guard His house against the army passing through. Alexander marched past Jerusalem without destroying it. Josephus says he honoured the high priest and was shown Daniel's prophecy about Greece.

title: Tyre's stones and timber laid in the midst of the water
fulfilment: History: Alexander's causeway to island Tyre
summary: Ezekiel foretold many nations against Tyre, her stones and dust thrown into the sea and the site left like bare rock. Alexander scraped the ruins of mainland Tyre into the sea to build a causeway to the island. Johnson's book frames Tyre's fall as 587-326 BC.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), period headings (book text past c. 711 BC not readable; no item numbers)

title: Sons of Zion raised against the sons of Greece
summary: God would arm the sons of Zion against the sons of Greece (Javan). The Maccabees rose against the Greek Seleucid king Antiochus IV and won.

title: An altar to the LORD in the midst of Egypt
summary: Isaiah saw Egyptian cities speaking the language of Canaan and an altar to the LORD in Egypt. Onias IV built a Jewish temple at Leontopolis and, Josephus says, appealed to this passage. The worldwide turning of Egypt is still future.

title: A mighty king will rule with great dominion
summary: After the Persian kings a mighty king would rise and do as he pleased. Johnson's map gives Alexander 326-323 BC (secular reign 336-323 BC).

title: His kingdom broken while he is at his height
summary: As soon as he stood up, his kingdom would be broken. Alexander died at 32, only a few years after reaching full power.

title: Kingdom not passed to his descendants
fulfilment: History: murders of Alexander IV and Heracles
summary: The kingdom would not go to his posterity. Alexander's sons, Alexander IV and Heracles, were murdered, and the line ended.

title: Kingdom divided toward the four winds
summary: The empire would be divided to the four winds and ruled by others. Johnson names the four as Seleucus Nicator, Cassander, Lysimachus and Ptolemy.

title: King of the South strong; one of his princes stronger
fulfilment: History: Ptolemy I and Seleucus I
summary: The king of the South (Ptolemy I of Egypt) would be strong, but one of his commanders would become stronger. Seleucus, once Ptolemy's officer, built the larger Seleucid kingdom. Johnson's dates: Ptolemy I 323-285 BC, Seleucus 311-280 BC.

title: King's daughter of the South given to the North, but not retaining power
summary: A daughter of the southern king would marry the northern king to seal an alliance, but she would not keep her position. Berenice married Antiochus II. After his death Laodice had her and her son killed, as Seleucus II took the throne (Johnson: 246 BC).

title: A branch of her roots attacks the North
fulfilment: History: Third Syrian War, Ptolemy III
summary: One from her family line would attack the northern king's fortress and prevail. Her brother Ptolemy III Euergetes invaded Seleucid territory to avenge her (Johnson: 246-221 BC).

title: Their gods and precious vessels carried to Egypt
fulfilment: History: Canopus Decree records returned idols
summary: The southern king would carry off their gods, images and treasures to Egypt. Ptolemy III brought back statues the Persians had taken. Johnson's footnote ties these to Cambyses' plunder of 525 BC.

title: King of the North invades the South and returns home
summary: The king of the North would come into the South's kingdom but go back to his own land. Seleucus II's counter-attack on Egypt failed.

title: His sons stir up a great army and overflow
fulfilment: History: Seleucus III and Antiochus III
summary: His sons would gather great forces and sweep through to the southern fortress. Seleucus III and then Antiochus III went to war, and Antiochus advanced to Raphia (Johnson: by 218 BC).

title: King of the South defeats the great northern army
summary: The enraged southern king would fight the northern multitude and win. Ptolemy IV beat Antiochus III at Raphia in 217 BC.

title: The southern victor kills tens of thousands but does not prevail
summary: After casting down many thousands, the southern king would not press his advantage. Ptolemy IV made peace instead of conquering Syria. Johnson cites Polybius for over 10,000 dead.

title: After some years the North returns with a greater army
summary: The northern king would return years later with a larger army and great riches. When Ptolemy IV died, Antiochus III attacked his child heir (Johnson: about 13 years after 217 BC).

title: Many rise against the South; violent men of your people
summary: Many would rise against the southern king, and lawless men among the Jews would try to fulfil the vision but fall. Philip V allied with Antiochus III, and some Jews sided with Antiochus. The Egyptian general Scopas crushed the revolt.

title: North takes a well-fortified city
fulfilment: History: Battle of Panium; siege of Sidon
summary: The northern king would besiege and capture a fortified city, and the South's best troops could not stop him. Antiochus III won at Panium and forced Scopas to surrender at Sidon.

title: He stands in the Glorious Land
summary: The northern king would do as he pleased and stand in the Beautiful Land. Judea passed from Ptolemaic to Seleucid control (Johnson: by 197 BC).

title: He gives his daughter to the South, but she does not side with him
fulfilment: History: Cleopatra I marries Ptolemy V
summary: He would give a daughter in marriage to undermine the kingdom, but she would not serve his plan. Antiochus III married Cleopatra I to Ptolemy V, and she sided with her husband (Johnson: 194 BC).

title: He turns to the coastlands; a commander ends his insolence
fulfilment: History: Lucius Scipio defeats Antiochus III
summary: He would turn to the coastlands and take many, but a commander would stop him and turn his scorn back on him. Rome under Scipio Asiaticus defeated Antiochus at Magnesia.

title: He stumbles and falls and is not found
fulfilment: History: death of Antiochus III at Elymais
summary: He would go back to his own fortresses, stumble and fall. Antiochus III was killed while plundering a temple of Bel in Elymais (Johnson: 187 BC).

title: A raiser of taxes, destroyed neither in anger nor in battle
summary: His successor would send a tax collector through the glorious kingdom and then die, not in anger or battle. Seleucus IV sent Heliodorus to seize the Temple treasury and was later poisoned by him (Johnson: 187-175 BC).

title: A contemptible person seizes the kingdom by flatteries
summary: A despised man without rightful claim would take the throne by intrigue. Antiochus IV pushed aside the heir Demetrius I (Johnson: reigned 175-164 BC).

title: The prince of the covenant broken
summary: Armies would be swept away before him, and the prince of the covenant would be broken. Johnson identifies this prince as the deposed high priest Onias III, who was murdered.

title: He works deceitfully after the league and scatters the spoil
summary: After making alliances he would act deceitfully and hand out plunder as his fathers never did. Johnson says Antiochus deceived Rome into recognising him. Ancient writers note his lavish handouts.

title: Great army against the South; the South betrayed by his own
summary: He would march against the South with a great army, and the southern king would be undone by the counsel of those who ate at his table. Antiochus IV defeated Ptolemy VI, whose advisers had pushed him into the war.

title: Two kings speak lies at one table
fulfilment: History: Antiochus IV and Ptolemy VI at Memphis
summary: Both kings, bent on mischief, would lie to each other at one table. Antiochus held Ptolemy VI as a 'guest' while each plotted against the other.

title: He returns with riches, his heart against the holy covenant
summary: Coming home with great wealth, he would act against the holy covenant. Antiochus plundered the Temple in Jerusalem (Johnson: 169 BC, after deposing Jason).

title: Ships of Kittim come against him; he turns back grieved
summary: On a second invasion of the South it would not go as before: ships from Kittim would come against him. The Roman envoy Popillius Laenas drew a circle around Antiochus and made him leave Egypt.

title: Sanctuary profaned, daily sacrifice ended, abomination set up
summary: His forces would defile the sanctuary, stop the daily sacrifice and set up the abomination that makes desolate. Antiochus put a pagan altar on the Temple altar (secular: 15/25 Kislev 167 BC). Johnson's map heads this 165 BC and sees it as a type of the Antichrist.

title: Those who forsake the covenant corrupted by flatteries
summary: He would favour those who forsook the covenant and corrupt them with flattery. Hellenising Jews such as Jason and Menelaus took his side and abandoned the Law.

title: People who know their God are strong and do exploits
summary: Those who knew their God would stand firm and act. Mattathias and Judas Maccabeus led the revolt and retook the Temple (Johnson: Maccabean era 164-64 BC).

title: The wise fall by sword, flame, captivity and spoil many days
summary: The wise among the people would teach many yet fall by sword, flame and captivity for many days, to be refined until the end. Johnson places this in the Roman dispersion (AD 70 and AD 130-1948). Chuck Smith applies verse 33 to the Maccabees.

title: Little horn grows toward south, east and the Pleasant Land
fulfilment: History: Antiochus IV's campaigns in Egypt, Persia, Judea
summary: From one of the four horns a little horn would grow great toward the south, the east and the Pleasant Land. Antiochus IV campaigned in Egypt, in the east, and in Judea.

title: Daily sacrifice taken away and sanctuary cast down
summary: The horn would set itself against the Prince of the host, remove the daily sacrifice and throw down the sanctuary. Antiochus banned the sacrifices and defiled the Temple. Chuck Smith says he offered a pig on the altar.

title: After 2,300 evenings and mornings the sanctuary is cleansed
summary: Daniel heard that the sanctuary would be restored after 2,300 evenings and mornings. Judas Maccabeus cleansed and rededicated the Temple on 25 Kislev 164 BC, the origin of Hanukkah. Chuck Smith rejects reading the figure as 2,300 years.

title: A fierce king, mighty but not by his own power, destroys the holy people
summary: In the latter part of the four kingdoms a fierce, cunning king would rise and destroy many of the holy people. Antiochus' forces massacred Jerusalemites and enslaved others. Chuck Smith and Johnson also see a future Antichrist in him.

title: He will be broken without human hand
summary: This king would stand against the Prince of princes but be broken without human hand. Antiochus IV died of illness in Persia, not in battle (Johnson: 164 BC).

title: Ships from Kittim will afflict Asshur and Eber

given.label: c. 1437 BC (end of the wilderness years)

fulfilment: History: Rome annexes Syria and takes Jerusalem
summary: Balaam foresaw ships from Kittim afflicting Asshur and Eber. Johnson reads Kittim as Rome, Asshur as Syria and Eber as Israel: Pompey ended the Seleucid kingdom and took Jerusalem.

title: Seed of the woman will crush the serpent's head
summary: God promised that a descendant of the woman would crush the serpent while being wounded himself. Christians see this begun at the cross and finished at Satan's final defeat. This is #1 in Johnson's book.

sources.name: Ancient Prophecies Revealed, #1 (Curse of the Fall and promise of a Redeemer)

title: All nations blessed through Abraham's seed
summary: God promised that through Abraham's offspring all nations would be blessed. Paul says this singular Seed is Christ, a descendant of Abraham.

title: The promised line will come through Isaac
summary: The covenant line was to run through Isaac, not Ishmael. Luke's genealogy traces Jesus through Isaac.

title: A Star out of Jacob, a Sceptre out of Israel

given.label: c. 1437 BC (end of the wilderness years)

summary: Balaam saw a Star from Jacob and a ruler from Israel in the distant future. The Magi followed a star to the newborn King of the Jews. The ruling and crushing parts look ahead to His reign.

title: Messiah will come from the tribe of Judah
summary: Jacob gave the sceptre to Judah. Jesus was born in the tribe of Judah.

title: Sceptre not to depart from Judah until Shiloh comes

fulfilled.label: c. AD 6-7 (Archelaus deposed; Roman direct rule)

fulfilment: History: Judea becomes a Roman province
summary: Judah's ruling authority would last until Shiloh came. Evangelical writers note Messiah was born before Judea lost its self-rule: Archelaus was deposed in AD 6 and Rome took direct control, including capital cases.

sources.name: Josh McDowell, Evidence That Demands a Verdict, messianic prophecy list (as summarised online)

title: A shoot from the stump of Jesse
summary: A Branch would grow from Jesse's line, and the nations would seek Him. Jesus was born in Jesse's family line through David.

title: David's seed to have an everlasting throne
summary: God promised David a descendant whose throne would last forever. Jesus was born of David's line and announced as heir to David's throne. His visible reign is still future. This is #38 in Johnson's book.

sources.name: Ancient Prophecies Revealed, #38 (David's throne will continue forever)

title: A righteous Branch for David, called the LORD our Righteousness
summary: God would raise a righteous Branch for David who would reign and be called the LORD our Righteousness. The New Testament presents Jesus as this Son of David. His reign over the land is still future.

title: A virgin shall conceive and bear a son
summary: Isaiah gave the sign of a virgin bearing a son. Matthew and Luke record Jesus conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of the virgin Mary.

sources.name: Josh McDowell, Evidence That Demands a Verdict, messianic prophecy list (as summarised online)

title: His name shall be called Immanuel
summary: The child would be called Immanuel, 'God with us'. Matthew applies the title to Jesus at his birth.

sources.name: Josh McDowell, Evidence That Demands a Verdict, messianic prophecy list (as summarised online)

title: A child born, a son given: Mighty God, Prince of Peace
summary: Isaiah foresaw a child with divine titles who would sit on David's throne forever. The Gospels present Jesus as the incarnate Son. His unending government is still to be fully seen.

title: Messiah to be born in Bethlehem Ephrathah
summary: Micah named little Bethlehem as birthplace of Israel's ruler. Jesus was born there, and the scribes quoted this verse to Herod. Johnson dates the birth to 2 BC.

sources.name: Josh McDowell, Evidence That Demands a Verdict, messianic prophecy list (as summarised online)

title: The ruler's goings forth are from everlasting
summary: The ruler from Bethlehem would have origins from of old, from eternity. The New Testament says the one born in Bethlehem existed before all things.

sources.name: Josh McDowell, Evidence That Demands a Verdict, messianic prophecy list (as summarised online)

title: Lo, I come: to do Your will (body prepared)
summary: The psalmist says sacrifices did not satisfy God and one comes to do His will. Hebrews applies this to Christ's coming into the world.

title: David's son is David's Lord
summary: David calls the coming king 'my Lord'. The angels announced Jesus as Christ the Lord, and Jesus used the verse to show the Messiah was more than David's son.

sources.name: Josh McDowell, Evidence That Demands a Verdict, messianic prophecy list (as summarised online)

title: The glory of the latter house greater than the former
summary: Haggai promised the rebuilt Temple would have greater glory than Solomon's. Evangelicals see this in the Messiah himself entering the Second Temple, from his presentation as an infant onward.

title: Kings will bring gifts and bow before him
summary: Kings from distant lands would bring gifts of gold and frankincense. Magi from the east brought gold, frankincense and myrrh to the child Jesus. The worldwide homage is still future.

title: Rachel weeping for her children
summary: Jeremiah pictured Rachel weeping in Ramah for her lost children. Matthew applies it to Herod's slaughter of the infants of Bethlehem.

sources.name: Josh McDowell, Evidence That Demands a Verdict, messianic prophecy list (as summarised online)

title: Out of Egypt I called my son
summary: Hosea recalls God calling His son Israel out of Egypt. Matthew sees this repeated when Jesus was brought back from Egypt after Herod died.

title: He shall be called a Nazarene (the Branch)
summary: The prophets spoke of a lowly Branch (Hebrew netzer). Jesus grew up in obscure Nazareth, and Matthew says this fulfilled what the prophets said.

title: Gabriel: Elizabeth will bear a son named John

given.label: c. 3 BC (in the course of Abijah)

fulfilled.label: c. Passover, 2 BC (Johnson: John born about Nisan 15)

summary: Gabriel told the elderly priest Zacharias that his barren wife would bear a son, to be named John. John was born and named as foretold. Johnson places his birth near Passover, about six months before Jesus.

title: Zacharias will be mute until the promise is fulfilled
summary: Because he doubted, Zacharias would be unable to speak until the birth. His speech came back the moment he wrote 'His name is John'.

title: Gabriel: Mary will conceive the Son of the Highest
summary: Gabriel told Mary she would conceive by the Holy Spirit and bear a son named Jesus, Son of the Most High. The child was born and named Jesus.

title: Angel to Joseph: call His name Jesus, He will save His people
summary: An angel told Joseph that Mary's child was from the Holy Spirit and was to be named Jesus. Joseph took Mary as his wife and named the child Jesus.

title: Shepherds will find the babe in a manger
summary: The angel gave the shepherds a sign: a newborn wrapped in cloths, lying in a manger. They went to Bethlehem and found him just so.

title: Simeon will not die before seeing the Lord's Christ
summary: The Spirit had promised Simeon he would see the Messiah before he died. He held the infant Jesus in the Temple and blessed God.

title: A sword will pierce Mary's soul; the child set for falling and rising
summary: Simeon said the child would be opposed and a sword would pierce his mother's soul. Mary stood at the cross and watched her son die.

title: Flee to Egypt, for Herod will seek the child
summary: An angel warned that Herod would seek to kill the child. Herod sent soldiers to kill the boys of Bethlehem, and the family returned only after he died.

title: A voice crying in the wilderness: prepare the way
summary: A herald would cry in the wilderness to prepare the LORD's way. John the Baptist preached in the Judean wilderness and called himself that voice.

title: My messenger will prepare the way before Me
summary: God would send a messenger ahead of His coming. Jesus said John the Baptist was that messenger.

title: Elijah the prophet sent before the day of the LORD
summary: God would send Elijah before the great day of the LORD. Jesus said John came in Elijah's spirit, and Johnson ties John to Elijah's cup at the Seder. Many also expect a future Elijah (Revelation 11).

title: Behold the Lamb of God (Passover lamb identified)
summary: John called Jesus the Lamb of God who takes away the world's sin. Johnson notes Jesus died at 3 PM on Nisan 14, when the Passover lambs were slain.

title: The coming one will baptize with the Holy Spirit
summary: John said one mightier than he would baptize with the Holy Spirit. The Spirit came on the disciples at Pentecost.

title: I will put My Spirit upon Him (My servant)
summary: God's chosen Servant would have the Spirit on him. At Jesus' baptism the Spirit came down like a dove and the Father spoke His approval. Johnson dates the ministry from AD 28.

title: You are My Son, today I have begotten You
summary: God declares the anointed king His Son. The Father's voice at the baptism echoes this, and Acts applies it to the resurrection.

title: Galilee of the nations will see a great light
summary: The despised lands of Zebulun and Naphtali, Galilee of the Gentiles, would see a great light. Jesus based his ministry in Capernaum and preached throughout Galilee.

title: Anointed to preach good news to the poor and proclaim liberty
summary: The Spirit-anointed one would bring good news, healing and freedom. In Nazareth Jesus read this and said 'today this is fulfilled', stopping before 'the day of vengeance', which is still future.

title: Eyes of the blind opened, deaf hear, lame leap
summary: When God came to save, the blind, deaf, lame and mute would be healed. Jesus pointed John's disciples to exactly these healings.

title: He took our infirmities and bore our sicknesses
summary: The Servant would carry the people's griefs and sicknesses. Matthew applies this to Jesus' healings in Capernaum.

title: I will open my mouth in parables
summary: The psalmist would speak in parables and dark sayings from of old. Jesus taught the crowds in parables, which Matthew says fulfilled this.

title: A Prophet like Moses raised up from among the brethren

given.label: c. 1436 BC (Moses on the plains of Moab)

summary: God would raise a prophet like Moses whom Israel must hear. Peter and Stephen preached that Jesus is that Prophet.

title: He will not cry out, break a bruised reed, or quench smoking flax
summary: The Servant would be quiet and gentle with the weak. Jesus healed the crowds and told them not to make him known, as Matthew notes.

title: A light to the Gentiles, salvation to the ends of the earth

fulfilled.label: c. AD 47 (Paul and Barnabas turn to Gentiles)

summary: The Servant would be a light to the nations as well as Israel. The gospel went out to the Gentiles, and Paul quoted this when he turned to them. Its spread to the ends of the earth continues.

title: Zeal for Your house has eaten me up

fulfilled.label: c. AD 29 (first Passover of the ministry)

summary: The psalmist was consumed by zeal for God's house. Jesus drove the money changers out of the Temple, and his disciples remembered this verse. Johnson links the cleansing to the Passover search for leaven.

title: A stranger to my brothers, an alien to my mother's children
summary: The sufferer would be estranged from his own brothers. Jesus' brothers did not believe in him during his ministry.

title: Despised and rejected of men
summary: The Servant would be despised, rejected and held in low esteem. Jesus' own people and leaders rejected him. Chuck Smith ties this to Jesus' rejection.

title: Who has believed our report?
summary: Isaiah asks who would believe the message about the arm of the LORD. Despite many signs, most did not believe Jesus, which John says fulfilled Isaiah.

title: Hearing they will not understand; seeing they will not perceive
summary: Isaiah was told the people would hear without understanding. Jesus said this explained his parables, and Paul repeated it in Rome.

title: They hated me without a cause
summary: The righteous sufferer would be hated for no reason. Jesus said his enemies' hatred fulfilled this psalm.

title: A stone of stumbling and rock of offence
summary: The LORD would be a stumbling stone to both houses of Israel. The apostles say Israel's leaders stumbled over Jesus.

title: A priest forever after the order of Melchizedek
summary: God swore that David's Lord would be a priest forever like Melchizedek. Hebrews says Jesus entered heaven as that high priest.

sources.name: Josh McDowell, Evidence That Demands a Verdict, messianic prophecy list (as summarised online)

title: Some standing here will see the Son of Man in His kingdom
summary: Jesus said some present would not die before seeing him in kingdom glory. Six days later Peter, James and John saw him transfigured.

title: The first fish caught will have a coin for the tax
summary: Jesus told Peter that the first fish he caught would have a coin in its mouth to pay the Temple tax for both of them.

title: Lazarus' sickness is not to death; I go to wake him
summary: Jesus said Lazarus' illness would not end in death and that he would wake him. After four days in the tomb, Lazarus came out alive.

title: Caiaphas: one man should die for the nation
summary: The high priest said one man should die for the people, and John says he unknowingly prophesied Jesus' death for the nation and God's scattered children.

title: Street and wall rebuilt in troubled times (first seven weeks)

given.label: 536 BC (1st year of Darius the Mede)

summary: Jerusalem would be rebuilt with street and wall in troublous times during the first seven weeks. Nehemiah rebuilt the walls under opposition after the decree Johnson dates to Nisan 444 BC.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, The Rapture (Daniel's seventy weeks chapter)

title: 69 weeks (483 years) from the decree to Messiah the Prince

given.label: 536 BC (1st year of Darius the Mede)

summary: From the decree to rebuild Jerusalem to Messiah the Prince would be 69 weeks of years. Johnson, following Anderson, counts 173,880 days from Nisan 444 BC to 6 April AD 32, the triumphal entry. Chuck Smith and Skip Heitzig give the same end date (they start from 445 BC).

sources.name: Ken Johnson, The Rapture (Daniel's seventy weeks chapter)
Skip Heitzig, God's Precision (Connection devotional, Jan 2025)

title: After the 62 weeks Messiah will be cut off, but not for Himself

given.label: 536 BC (1st year of Darius the Mede)

summary: After the 69 weeks the Anointed One would be cut off, having nothing. Jesus was crucified days after the entry. Johnson dates his death to Nisan 14 AD 32 (3957 AM) and links 11Q13's timing to it.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, The Rapture (Daniel's seventy weeks chapter)
Ken Johnson, dsscalendar.org Onah anchor table (Messiah's death 3957 AM / AD 32)

title: Seventy weeks: to make reconciliation for iniquity

given.label: 536 BC (1st year of Darius the Mede)

summary: The seventy weeks would end sin, atone for iniquity and bring in everlasting righteousness. Atonement was made at the cross. Johnson holds the 70th week is a future seven-year Tribulation after a gap.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, The Rapture (Daniel's seventy weeks chapter)

title: Your King comes, lowly, riding on a donkey's colt
summary: Zion's King would come to her humble and riding a donkey's colt. Jesus rode into Jerusalem on a colt to shouts of Hosanna, which Johnson dates to 6 April AD 32.

sources.name: Skip Heitzig, God's Precision (Connection devotional, Jan 2025)
Ken Johnson, The Rapture (Daniel's seventy weeks chapter)

title: Hosanna: blessed is He who comes in the name of the LORD
summary: The festival psalm greets the one coming in the LORD's name. The crowds sang these words as Jesus entered Jerusalem.

title: Out of the mouths of babes You have perfected praise
summary: God draws praise from children and infants. Children in the Temple cried 'Hosanna to the Son of David', and Jesus quoted this psalm to the angry priests.

title: Passover lamb chosen on the 10th day and inspected
summary: The Passover lamb was chosen on Nisan 10 and kept until the 14th. Johnson notes Jesus presented himself in Jerusalem and the Temple on Nisan 10 and was examined and found without fault.

sources.name: Skip Heitzig, God's Precision (Connection devotional, Jan 2025)

title: The Lord will suddenly come to His temple
summary: The Lord whom they sought would suddenly come to His Temple and purify it. Jesus entered the Temple and drove out the traders. The refining judgment is also future.

title: You will find a colt tied, on which no man has sat
summary: Jesus sent two disciples to a village where they would find an unridden colt, and told them what the owners would say. It happened exactly so.

title: The stone the builders rejected becomes the cornerstone
summary: A stone rejected by the builders would become the head of the corner. Jesus applied this to himself, and Peter preached that the rejected, crucified Jesus was raised to be the cornerstone.

title: The kingdom will be taken from you and given to a nation bearing fruit
summary: In the parable of the tenants, Jesus warned the leaders that the vineyard would be taken from them and they would be destroyed. The gospel went to the Gentiles and the Temple leadership fell in AD 70.

title: Anointed beforehand for burial
summary: Jesus said Mary's anointing at Bethany prepared his body for burial. Within a week he was dead and buried.

title: After two days is the Passover, and the Son of Man is betrayed
summary: Jesus said that at the coming Passover he would be handed over to be crucified. He was arrested and crucified at that Passover.

title: Delivered to the Gentiles to be mocked, scourged and crucified
summary: On the road to Jerusalem Jesus said the chief priests would condemn him and hand him to the Gentiles to be mocked, spat on, scourged and crucified. Every detail followed.

title: The Son of Man must be lifted up (death by crucifixion)
summary: Like Moses' bronze serpent, the Son of Man would be lifted up, which pointed to death by crucifixion. A Roman cross rather than Jewish stoning fulfilled it, as John notes.

title: They will strike the Judge of Israel with a rod on the cheek
summary: Micah saw the ruler of Israel struck on the cheek. Johnson says it was fulfilled in AD 32 when the Roman soldiers struck and mocked Jesus.

title: My own familiar friend, who ate my bread, lifted his heel against me
summary: A trusted friend who shared bread would turn against him. Judas, one of the Twelve, ate with Jesus and betrayed him that night.

sources.name: Josh McDowell, Evidence That Demands a Verdict, messianic prophecy list (as summarised online)

title: One of you will betray Me
summary: At the Last Supper Jesus said one of the Twelve would betray him and pointed out Judas with the dipped bread. Within hours Judas led the arresting party.

title: Priced at thirty pieces of silver
summary: The rejected shepherd's wages were weighed out as thirty pieces of silver. The chief priests paid Judas thirty pieces of silver to betray Jesus.

sources.name: Josh McDowell, Evidence That Demands a Verdict, messianic prophecy list (as summarised online)

title: The silver thrown down in the house of the LORD
summary: The thirty pieces were thrown into the house of the LORD. A remorseful Judas threw the money down in the Temple.

sources.name: Josh McDowell, Evidence That Demands a Verdict, messianic prophecy list (as summarised online)

title: The silver given for the potter
summary: The money was cast to the potter. The priests used Judas' silver to buy the potter's field as a burial ground for foreigners.

sources.name: Josh McDowell, Evidence That Demands a Verdict, messianic prophecy list (as summarised online)

title: Let another take his office
summary: The psalm says another would take the betrayer's office. Peter cited it, and Matthias was chosen to replace Judas among the Twelve.

title: A man carrying a pitcher will show you a large upper room
summary: Jesus told two disciples to follow a man carrying a water jar to a house with a furnished upper room. They found everything as he said.

title: Strike the Shepherd and the sheep will scatter
summary: God's Shepherd would be struck and the flock scattered. Jesus quoted this at the Last Supper, and when he was arrested all the disciples fled.

title: Before the rooster crows you will deny Me three times
summary: Jesus told Peter he would deny him three times before the rooster crowed (twice, in Mark). That night Peter denied him three times, then the rooster crowed.

title: After I am raised I will go before you into Galilee
summary: Jesus promised to meet his scattered disciples in Galilee after his resurrection. He appeared to them on a mountain and by the Sea of Galilee.

title: False witnesses rise up against me
summary: False witnesses would rise up against the righteous one. At the night trial before the Sanhedrin, false witnesses accused Jesus, but their stories did not agree.

title: As a sheep before its shearers is silent, He opened not His mouth
summary: The Servant would be led like a lamb to slaughter without protest. Jesus stayed silent before the high priest, Pilate and Herod. Chuck Smith points to his silence before Pilate.

title: I gave My back to the smiters and hid not My face from spitting
summary: The Servant would give his back to beatings and his face to spitting. Jesus was spat on, struck and scourged.

sources.name: Josh McDowell, Evidence That Demands a Verdict, messianic prophecy list (as summarised online)

title: His appearance marred more than any man
summary: The Servant would be disfigured beyond human likeness. Chuck Smith links this to the beatings Jesus took while blindfolded and to the crown of thorns.

title: By His stripes we are healed
summary: The Servant would be wounded and whipped for others' sins. Jesus was scourged before crucifixion. Johnson ties the striped, pierced Passover matzah to this verse.

title: Kings and rulers gather against the LORD's Anointed
summary: Rulers would plot together against God's Anointed. The early church saw Herod, Pilate, the Gentiles and Israel's leaders join against Jesus.

title: All who see Me mock: He trusted in the LORD, let Him deliver Him
summary: Onlookers would shake their heads and taunt him for trusting God. At the cross passers-by and priests mocked Jesus in almost the psalm's own words.

sources.name: Josh McDowell, Evidence That Demands a Verdict, messianic prophecy list (as summarised online)

title: They pierced My hands and My feet
summary: The sufferer's hands and feet would be pierced, written centuries before crucifixion was used. Jesus was nailed to the cross and later showed the wounds. Johnson and Chuck Smith both cite it.

sources.name: Josh McDowell, Evidence That Demands a Verdict, messianic prophecy list (as summarised online)

title: All My bones are out of joint; My heart like wax
summary: The psalm describes bones pulled out of joint and a melting heart. Chuck Smith explains that crucifixion dislocates the joints as the muscles give out.

title: My tongue cleaves to My jaws
summary: The sufferer's strength would dry up and his tongue stick to his mouth. On the cross Jesus said 'I thirst'.

title: They divide My garments and cast lots for My clothing
summary: His clothes would be shared out and lots cast for his garment. The soldiers divided Jesus' clothes and gambled for his seamless tunic.

title: My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?
summary: The psalm opens with the cry of the forsaken one. Jesus cried these words from the cross about the ninth hour.

title: He was numbered with the transgressors
summary: The Servant would be counted among criminals. Jesus was crucified between two robbers. Chuck Smith notes the two thieves.

title: He made intercession for the transgressors
summary: The Servant would pray for transgressors. On the cross Jesus prayed 'Father, forgive them'. Chuck Smith cites this.

title: The LORD laid on Him the iniquity of us all
summary: The Servant would be wounded for others' transgressions and made an offering for sin. The apostles teach that Jesus bore our sins in his body on the cross.

title: Cut off out of the land of the living
summary: The Servant would be taken by oppression and judgment and cut off. Chuck Smith links this with Daniel 9:26 and the crucifixion.

title: They gave Me gall for food and vinegar for My thirst
summary: His enemies would give him gall and sour wine. Jesus was offered wine mixed with gall, then vinegar on a sponge.

title: My friends stand aloof; my kinsmen stand far off
summary: The sufferer's friends would stand at a distance. Jesus' acquaintances and the women watched the crucifixion from afar.

title: I will make the sun go down at noon
summary: God would darken the earth in broad daylight. Darkness covered the land from the sixth to the ninth hour while Jesus hung on the cross. Many also see a future day-of-the-LORD fulfilment.

title: Into Your hand I commit My spirit
summary: The psalmist entrusts his spirit to God. Jesus' last words on the cross were these.

title: Not a bone of Him shall be broken
summary: No bone of the Passover lamb was to be broken, and God keeps the righteous one's bones. The soldiers broke the thieves' legs but not Jesus', since he was already dead.

title: The Passover lamb slain on Nisan 14 between the evenings
summary: The Passover lamb was killed in the afternoon of Nisan 14. Johnson teaches that Jesus died at 3 PM on Thursday, Nisan 14, AD 32, the hour the lambs were slain.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, dsscalendar.org Onah anchor table (Messiah's death 3957 AM / AD 32)

title: He who is hanged on a tree is accursed

given.label: c. 1436 BC (Moses on the plains of Moab)

summary: The Law cursed anyone hanged on a tree and required burial the same day. Paul says Christ became a curse for us on the tree, and the body was taken down before evening.

title: They shall look on Me whom they pierced
summary: Jerusalem would look on the one they pierced and mourn. A soldier pierced Jesus' side, and John cites this verse. Chuck Smith places Israel's national mourning in the future.

sources.name: Josh McDowell, Evidence That Demands a Verdict, messianic prophecy list (as summarised online)

title: With the rich in His death
summary: Though meant to be buried with the wicked, the Servant would be with a rich man in his death. Jesus was buried in the new tomb of the wealthy Joseph of Arimathea.

sources.name: Josh McDowell, Evidence That Demands a Verdict, messianic prophecy list (as summarised online)

title: Feast of Unleavened Bread: the sinless one buried
summary: The Feast of Unleavened Bread began on Nisan 15. Johnson teaches that Jesus, sinless like unleavened bread, was buried as Nisan 15 began.

title: A new covenant with Israel and Judah
summary: God promised a new covenant, written on hearts, with sins forgiven. Jesus set it up in his blood at the Last Supper. Its full national application to Israel is still future.

title: God will provide Himself a lamb, on the mount of Moriah
summary: On Moriah Abraham said God would provide the lamb, and named the place 'the LORD will provide'. Christians see the Father giving His Son as the Lamb near the same mountains.

title: Daughters of Jerusalem, weep for yourselves and your children
summary: On the way to the cross Jesus told the mourning women to weep for themselves, because days would come when the barren would be called blessed. Jerusalem's siege brought famine and slaughter in AD 70.

sources.name: Josephus, The Wars of the Jews

title: You will not leave My soul in Sheol nor let Your Holy One see corruption
summary: David wrote that God's Holy One would not decay in the grave. Peter and Paul preached that David's tomb was still occupied but Jesus rose without decay.

title: After His soul's travail He will see His seed and prolong His days
summary: Having been made an offering for sin, the Servant would still live long and see his offspring. This implies life after death, fulfilled in the resurrection.

title: First Fruits waved the day after the Sabbath
summary: The first sheaf of harvest was waved before God the day after the Sabbath. Johnson teaches that First Fruits fell on Sunday, Nisan 17, AD 32, the day Christ rose. On the DSS calendar it is 26 Nisan, the barley First Fruits.

title: Three days and three nights in the heart of the earth
summary: Jesus said his only sign would be Jonah's: three days and nights in the earth. Johnson's Thursday crucifixion and Sunday resurrection are built to fit this sign.

title: Destroy this temple and in three days I will raise it up
summary: At his first Passover cleansing Jesus said he would raise up the 'temple' in three days, meaning his body. The disciples remembered this after he rose.

title: He must be killed and raised again the third day
summary: Jesus repeatedly told the Twelve he would suffer at Jerusalem, be killed and rise on the third day. The angels at the empty tomb reminded the women of these words.

title: I will declare Your name to My brethren
summary: Psalm 22 turns from suffering to the sufferer praising God among his brothers. On resurrection morning Jesus sent word to 'my brethren'.

title: You have ascended on high and led captivity captive
summary: God goes up on high, leading captives and giving gifts. Jesus ascended forty days after the resurrection. Johnson dates the ascension to 3957 AM (AD 32), and Paul applies the psalm to it.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, dsscalendar.org Enoch weeks (week 6: AD 32, AD 70, AD 132)

title: Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies Your footstool
summary: The LORD invites David's Lord to sit at His right hand. The apostles say Jesus is enthroned there now. Putting his enemies under his feet is still being completed.

sources.name: Josh McDowell, Evidence That Demands a Verdict, messianic prophecy list (as summarised online)

title: The Father will send the Comforter, the Holy Spirit
summary: Jesus promised the Spirit would come once he went away, and later 'not many days hence'. The Spirit fell on the disciples at Pentecost, which Johnson dates to 9 AM on a Sunday, AD 32.

title: I will pour out My Spirit on all flesh
summary: God would pour out His Spirit on all kinds of people. Peter said Pentecost was this, and Johnson calls it a partial fulfilment. The cosmic signs are still future.

title: Feast of Weeks: new offering fifty days after First Fruits
summary: Fifty days from First Fruits, Israel offered two leavened loaves of new grain. Johnson teaches the Spirit came on that day (Sivan 6, lunar reckoning) and 3,000 were saved, the birth of the Church. On the DSS calendar it is 15 Sivan.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), period headings (book text past c. 711 BC not readable; no item numbers)

title: I will build My church; the gates of Hades will not prevail
summary: Jesus said he would build his church and death's gates would not overcome it. The church was born at Pentecost and has lasted through every persecution. Johnson's book heads AD 32 with the birth of the Church.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), period headings (book text past c. 711 BC not readable; no item numbers)

title: Witnesses in Jerusalem, Judea, Samaria and the ends of the earth
summary: Jesus said the Spirit-empowered disciples would witness outward from Jerusalem. Acts traces the gospel from Jerusalem to Samaria and on to Rome. The spread to every nation continues.

title: You will be delivered to councils and scourged in synagogues
summary: Jesus warned that his messengers would be arrested, flogged and killed. The apostles were jailed and beaten by the Sanhedrin, and Stephen and James were killed.

title: James and John will drink of My cup
summary: Jesus told James and John they would share his suffering. James was beheaded by Herod Agrippa I (died AD 44), and John was exiled to Patmos.

title: Peter will stretch out his hands and be led where he would not go
summary: Jesus told Peter that when old he would stretch out his hands and be bound and led away, pointing to the death he would die. Early church tradition records Peter's crucifixion in Rome under Nero.

title: Paul will bear My name before Gentiles and kings and suffer much
summary: The Lord said Saul would carry His name to Gentiles, kings and Israel, and would suffer for it. Paul preached across the empire, stood before Felix, Festus and Agrippa, and endured much.

title: A great famine throughout the world
summary: The prophet Agabus foretold a great famine. Luke notes it came under Claudius, and Josephus describes severe famine in Judea at that time.

title: The Jews at Jerusalem will bind the owner of this belt
summary: Agabus tied his own hands and feet with Paul's belt and said Paul would be bound at Jerusalem and handed to the Gentiles. Paul was seized in the Temple and chained by the Romans.

title: You must also bear witness at Rome
summary: The Lord told the imprisoned Paul he would testify in Rome. Paul reached Rome and preached there for two years.

title: Ship lost but no life lost; aground on an island
summary: In the storm Paul said the ship would be lost but all aboard saved after running aground on an island. All 276 reached the shore of Malta.

title: Many will come in My name saying 'I am Christ'
summary: Jesus warned of false messiahs and prophets. Josephus records Theudas and 'the Egyptian', and Simon bar Kokhba was hailed as Messiah in AD 132. Jesus said more would come before the end.

title: People of the prince to come will destroy the city and sanctuary

given.label: 536 BC (1st year of Darius the Mede)

summary: After Messiah was cut off, the people of a coming prince would destroy Jerusalem and the Temple. Titus' Roman legions burned the Temple in AD 70 (Johnson: 3995 AM). Tradition dates the burning to 9/10 Av.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, The Rapture (Daniel's seventy weeks chapter)
Ken Johnson, dsscalendar.org Enoch weeks (week 6: AD 32, AD 70, AD 132)
Josephus, The Wars of the Jews

title: Its end with a flood; desolations determined

given.label: 536 BC (1st year of Darius the Mede)

fulfilment: History: Bar Kokhba war; Aelia Capitolina
summary: War and desolations would continue to the end like a flood. After AD 70 came the crushing of the Bar Kokhba revolt, when Hadrian expelled Jews from Jerusalem. Johnson dates the Roman dispersion to 4057 AM (AD 132).

sources.name: Ken Johnson, The Rapture (Daniel's seventy weeks chapter)
Ken Johnson, dsscalendar.org Enoch weeks (week 6: AD 32, AD 70, AD 132)

title: Not one stone will be left on another
summary: Looking at the Temple buildings, Jesus said every stone would be thrown down. Titus' troops burned the Temple and pulled it apart. Chuck Smith notes they prised the stones apart for the melted gold.

sources.name: Josephus, The Wars of the Jews

title: Your house is left to you desolate
summary: Mourning over Jerusalem, Jesus said its house would be left desolate. Chuck Smith reads this as the end of Israel's season of grace, followed by the AD 70 destruction.

title: All these things shall come upon this generation
summary: Jesus said judgment for the blood of the righteous would fall on that very generation. Jerusalem fell about 38 years later, within a generation.

sources.name: Josephus, The Wars of the Jews

title: Enemies will hem Jerusalem in and level it with its children
summary: Weeping over the city at the entry, Jesus said enemies would wall it in, hem it in on every side and dash it and its children to the ground, because it did not know the time of its visitation. Titus built a siege wall around Jerusalem and destroyed it.

sources.name: Josephus, The Wars of the Jews

title: When you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, its desolation is near
summary: Jesus said that armies surrounding Jerusalem would signal its coming desolation. Cestius Gallus besieged the city in AD 66, then pulled back unexpectedly. Titus encircled it in the spring of AD 70.

sources.name: Josephus, The Wars of the Jews

title: Then let those in Judea flee to the mountains
summary: Jesus told his followers to get out of Jerusalem as soon as the armies appeared. Eusebius records that the Jerusalem church, warned by a revelation, fled across the Jordan to Pella before the siege.

title: Great distress in the land and wrath on this people
summary: Jesus spoke of woe for nursing mothers and great distress in the land. Josephus describes the siege's famine and the deaths of over a million people. Matthew's wording also looks to the future Great Tribulation.

sources.name: Josephus, The Wars of the Jews

title: The king sent his armies, destroyed those murderers and burned their city
summary: In the wedding feast parable the king, angered at the killing of his servants, sends armies to burn their city. Rome burned Jerusalem in AD 70.

sources.name: Josephus, The Wars of the Jews

title: Led captive into all nations; Jerusalem trodden down by Gentiles
summary: Jesus said Jerusalem's people would die by the sword or be taken captive to every nation, and the city trodden down by Gentiles until the times of the Gentiles end. Josephus counts 97,000 captives in AD 70, and the dispersion followed in AD 132 (Johnson). Gentile rule over Jerusalem lasted into modern times.

sources.name: Josephus, The Wars of the Jews
Ken Johnson, dsscalendar.org Enoch weeks (week 6: AD 32, AD 70, AD 132)

title: Open your doors, O Lebanon, that fire may devour your cedars
summary: Zechariah calls on 'Lebanon' to open its doors to fire. The Talmud says the Temple doors opened by themselves forty years before the destruction and Yohanan ben Zakkai linked this verse to the Temple burning. The cedar-lined Temple burned in AD 70.

sources.name: Josephus, The Wars of the Jews

title: A nation from afar, swift as the eagle, of a language you do not understand

given.label: c. 1436 BC (Moses on the plains of Moab)

summary: Moses warned of a fierce foreign nation that would swoop like an eagle and besiege all their walled cities. Evangelical interpreters see this in Rome, whose standard was the eagle and whose legions besieged the cities of Judea in AD 67-70.

sources.name: Josephus, The Wars of the Jews

title: In the siege they will eat the flesh of their own children

given.label: c. 1436 BC (Moses on the plains of Moab)

summary: Moses foretold famine so severe in siege that even gentle mothers would eat their children. Josephus records this happening in the siege of AD 70 (it had also happened earlier, 2 Kings 6; Lamentations 4).

sources.name: Josephus, The Wars of the Jews

title: Brought back to Egypt in ships and sold, with no one to buy

given.label: c. 1436 BC (Moses on the plains of Moab)

fulfilment: Josephus, Wars 6.9.2; Jerome on Jeremiah 31 / Zechariah 11
summary: Israel would be sold as slaves until no buyer was left. Josephus says captives over seventeen were sent to the Egyptian mines in AD 70. After the Bar Kokhba revolt the slave markets were so glutted that Jews sold for almost nothing.

sources.name: Josephus, The Wars of the Jews

title: Scattered among all peoples, from one end of the earth to the other

given.label: c. 1436 BC (Moses on the plains of Moab)

fulfilment: History: Roman dispersion after AD 70 and AD 135
summary: If Israel broke the covenant they would be scattered among all nations and find no rest. After AD 70 and the Bar Kokhba war the Jewish people were dispersed worldwide. Johnson dates the dispersion to AD 132, lasting 1,816 years until 1948.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, The Rapture (Daniel's seventy weeks chapter)
Ken Johnson, dsscalendar.org Enoch weeks (week 6: AD 32, AD 70, AD 132)

title: Your cities waste, your sanctuaries desolate, your land desolate
summary: God warned that disobedience would leave the cities ruined, the sanctuaries desolate and the land empty while the people were scattered. Judea was devastated in AD 70 and again in AD 135, when Hadrian banned Jews from Jerusalem.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, The Rapture (Daniel's seventy weeks chapter)

title: Many days without king, prince, or sacrifice
fulfilment: History: sacrifice ends with the Temple, AD 70
summary: Israel would live many days without king, prince, sacrifice or ephod, then return to the LORD and David their king in the last days. Temple sacrifice ended in AD 70 and has not resumed. The return is future.

title: Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem a heap
summary: Micah warned that Zion would be ploughed like a field and the Temple hill overgrown. Jewish tradition says the Roman Turnus Rufus ploughed the Temple site, and Hadrian rebuilt the city as pagan Aelia Capitolina.

title: No survivor will remain of the house of Esau
fulfilment: Josephus, Wars 4.4-4.9; History: Idumeans vanish after AD 70
summary: Obadiah foretold that Edom would be consumed with no survivor. The Edomites (Idumeans) were absorbed into Judea under John Hyrcanus. After joining the Jewish revolt they disappeared as a people after AD 70.

sources.name: Josephus, The Wars of the Jews
